title: Isolation of adult mouse hippocampal neural stem cells for fluorescence loss in photobleaching assays
protocol: Euthanize the mice and isolate the brain.
Discard the olfactory bulbs.
Place two spatulas at the indicated arrows on the brain.
Force down the top straight spatula into the tissue.
Pull back the spatula in contact with the cerebellum, opening up the tissue where cerebrum and cerebellum meet.
Lift the hippocampus from the tissue using a curved spatula.
Cut the hippocampus from the rest of the brain using the edges of the spatula.
Place isolated hippocampi in cold HBSS w/o prepared earlier.
Separate and collect hippocampi in different 15 mL tubes based on age or genotype.
Keep the tubes containing hippocampi in HBSS w/o on ice.
Remove HBSS w/o from the tubes using a pipette.
Add prewarmed Enzyme Mix 1 gently to the tube, lifting tissue from the bottom.
Transfer Enzyme Mix 1 and hippocampi into a labeled C tube with a 2 mL pipette.
Close the C tube and flick it upside down to move hippocampi to the top of the tube.
Attach the C tube upside down onto the gentleMACS Dissociator and run program “m_brain_01.01”.
Take off the C tube after the program is complete, and flick it so that hippocampi are on the bottom.
Place the tube in the MACSmix Tube Rotator for 15 min at 37°C.
After the rotation, flip tissue to the lid by flicking the tube.
Attach the C tube upside down onto the gentleMACS Dissociator and run program “m_brain_02.01”.
Add Enzyme Mix 2 to the tube after the second dissociation program is complete.
Place the tube back on the MACSmix Tube Rotator for 10 min at 37°C.
After the rotation, flip tissue to the lid again by flicking the tube.
Attach the C tube upside down onto the gentleMACS Dissociator and run program “m_brain_03.01”.
Flip tissue to the bottom of the tube after the final dissociation program is complete.
Place the C tube in the MACSmix Tube Rotator and rotate slowly for 10 min at 37°C.
Centrifuge the C tube at 300g for 2 min at 20°C–25°C.
Pre-wet a 70μm cell strainer with 1 mL of warm HBSS w/.
Gently resuspend the pellet in its own supernatant using a 1 mL pipette.
Add all of the cell suspension to the pre-wetted cell strainer.
Rinse the C tube with 1 mL of warm HBSS w/ and add it to the cell strainer.
Wash the cell strainer with preheated HBSS w/.
Transfer the liquid from the cell strainer to a labeled 15 mL tube carefully.
Centrifuge the 15 mL tube at 300g for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of cold 7.2% sucrose solution and centrifuge at 850g for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully, resuspending the small pellet using a 200 μL pipette if necessary.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of warm HBSS w/ and centrifuge again at 300g for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Discard the supernatant after this spin.
Resuspend the final pellet in 1 mL of preheated culturing media.
Put 10 mL warm media in a 100x15mm dish.
Add the 1 mL media containing cells to the dish.
Take out 7 mL of media and spin it at 120g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Replace the media in the plate with 8 mL of freshly prepared culturing media.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of warm media.
Add the resuspended cells to the dish.
Feed the NSCs with fresh culturing media every 2-3 days.
Wait for isolated NSCs to form neurospheres and passage them as described.
Transfer the entire media in the plate to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 80g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of warm trypsin.
Incubate the tube at 37°C in a water-bath for 5 min.
Add 200 μL of trypsin inhibitor to the tube.
Lightly tap the tube.
Incubate the tube for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Use a 1 mL pipette to pipette the mixture with cells up and down approximately 20 times until the mixture turns cloudy.
Count the cells.
Add the volume corresponding to the number of cells required into a 15mL tube.
Centrifuge tube at 200g for 4 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in the Nucleofector Solution mixed with DNA earlier.
Transfer the resuspended NSCs to the cuvettes supplied with the Nucleofector kit.
Insert the cuvette into the Nucleofector device and run the program.
Immediately afterward, take the cuvette out and add 1 mL of prewarmed culturing media.
Plate 9x10^5 cells per well in the coated Nunc Lab-Tek 4-well chambered coverglass.
Plate the remaining cells in a 100x15mm dish with preheated culturing media.
Incubate the Nunc Lab-Tek 4-well chambered coverglass at 37°C for 16 hours.
Wash the cells twice with 1 mL of PBS to remove any dead cells and debris.
Add 1 mL of prewarmed media 3 hours before starting the FLIP assays.
Place the Nunc Lab-Tek 4-well chambered coverglass with NSCs on the stage.
Scan the cuvette to search for a cell in late metaphase using the eyepiece.
Adjust focus approximately 5–10 μm above the surface to locate cells in mitosis.
Perform FLIP assays to visualize diffusion dynamics of specific proteins in dividing NSCs.
Wait for the cell to start anaphase.
Select a region adjacent to the future cleavage furrow.
Bleach the selected region with appropriate laser power.
Acquire an image immediately after bleaching.
Rebleach the previously bleached region.
Repeat this process until there is no GFP signal visible between the two dividing compartments of the cell.
Save the image file as desired once FLIP has been performed on the specific cell.
Draw the regions of interest around the bleached and unbleached compartments using ImageJ.
Measure the area and intensity of all the regions of interest for both the bleached and unbleached compartments in the time-lapse.
Divide the fluorescence signal by the area to calculate the fluorescence intensities for both the bleached and the unbleached compartments for each frame.
Draw a region of interest around a dark region with no fluorescence.
Divide the fluorescence signal by the area to calculate the background fluorescence intensity.
Subtract the background fluorescence intensities for each frame from both the bleached and the unbleached fluorescence intensities.
Normalize the fluorescence intensities for the bleached and unbleached compartments using the pre-bleach intensity as a reference.
Calculate the time in seconds as (Frame N − 1) × 12, where 12 is the interval between frames.
Compile the normalized values for the bleached and unbleached compartments into a table.
Export the data from Excel into an XY table in Prism.
Fit the data to one-phase decay using Analyze > Non-linear Regression in Prism.
Set the y-intercept (Y0) to be equal to 100 under constraints.
Set the plateau value to 0 under constraints for data fitting.
Plot fitted curves and assess how well the data fits plotted curve.
Transfer results from Prism to an Excel sheet for both bleached and unbleached data.
Substitute the value of K into the equation X = ln((Y - Plateau)/(Y0 - Plateau)) / (-K).
Set Y at 80, with preassigned values of Plateau (100) and Y0 (0).
Calculate X for both bleached and unbleached compartments.
Use the calculated value of X to determine the time it takes for a compartment to reach 80% of original fluorescence.
Calculate barrier strength using Barrier Strength = (X Unbleached / X Bleached).
Determine total error in barrier strength calculations using Total Error for each compartment = -seK × ln((Y - Plateau)/(YO - Plateau)) / K^2.
Calculate the standard error for the bleached condition using the provided equation.
Calculate the standard error for the unbleached condition using the provided equation.
Sum the barrier index standard errors for both bleached and unbleached conditions to calculate the standard error in barrier strength.
